findings.text:
The new README paragraph says only `compose`, `lock` and `judge` take the mutation lock first. In hunsu.py, `@mutates_project` (which calls `project_mutation`, the one that does `with scratch_space("the mutation lock"): directory = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "hunsu-mutations")`) also wraps cmd_init, cmd_add, cmd_remove, cmd_install, cmd_link, cmd_unlink, cmd_dev, cmd_capability and cmd_role_add. In a read-only sandbox, `hunsu add X`, `init`, `install` and the others stop with the same `no writable temporary directory` diagnostic, but this paragraph and the 'Codex and the sandbox' sentence never mention them. A reader would think only those three commands are affected. The plan's own sentence is broader: "every command that changes the project first takes a lock file in a temporary directory (the mutation lock)". — tree: “+scratch files; `--remote` also needs scratch space for marketplace clones, and the mutation lock that `compose`, `lock`
+and `judge` take first lives in a temporary directory.”

disposition.delegated: Routine decision the owner delegated, no person read it: true — the README named three of the commands that take the mutation lock; task scratch-docs-lock now names every command that changes the project (init, add, remove, install, link/unlink, dev, capability, role add, compose, lock, judge)
